title: PSR2: tuned all-N streaming sieve with polynomial classical space

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single capped PSR2 algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 3/4 from independent ideal coset copies. On every execution branch its total charged sequential work satisfies T(N,s) = O(n^8 2^((3/2) sqrt(n log2 n))), uniformly with absolute constants, with the uniform bit-length representative envelope B(n) = n^8 2^((3/2) sqrt(n log2 n)) and exact growth index 1/2. This holds jointly with all other resource claims and the clean-input tolerance below for the same algorithm, including all failures, restarts, cutoff branches, source costs, controller bit operations, addressing and precision costs as applicable.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single capped PSR2 algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 3/4 from independent ideal coset copies. On every execution branch its peak classical workspace in bits satisfies S_C(N,s) = O(n^2), uniformly with absolute constants, with the uniform bit-length representative envelope B(n) = n^2 and exact growth index 0. This holds jointly with all other resource claims and the clean-input tolerance below for the same algorithm, including all failures, restarts, cutoff branches, source costs, controller bit operations, addressing and precision costs as applicable.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single capped PSR2 algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 3/4 from independent ideal coset copies. On every execution branch its peak quantum workspace in qubits satisfies S_Q(N,s) = O(n), uniformly with absolute constants, with the uniform bit-length representative envelope B(n) = n and exact growth index 0. This holds jointly with all other resource claims and the clean-input tolerance below for the same algorithm, including all failures, restarts, cutoff branches, source costs, controller bit operations, addressing and precision costs as applicable.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single capped PSR2 algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 3/4 from independent ideal coset copies. On every execution branch its total acquired source copies, including all discards and failed attempts satisfies Q(N,s) = O(n^2 2^((3/4) sqrt(n log2 n))), uniformly with absolute constants, with the uniform bit-length representative envelope B(n) = n^2 2^((3/4) sqrt(n log2 n)) and exact growth index 1/2. This holds jointly with all other resource claims and the clean-input tolerance below for the same algorithm, including all failures, restarts, cutoff branches, source costs, controller bit operations, addressing and precision costs as applicable.

For the same capped PSR2 algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, the proved fractional tolerance is epsilon(n)=0: every acquired source copy is independent and ideal. Under this promise full-secret recovery succeeds with unconditional probability at least 3/4 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance or impossibility of greater tolerance is asserted.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
